South Africa. . Its national anthem starts with Nkosi Sikelele iAfrika, a Xhosa hymn that means "God bless Africa." In translation, it was adopted as the national anthem by Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania and Namibia. In the apartheid years, the hymn Nkosi Sikelele became a symbol of protest against the regime. When Mandela became president, it acquired joint status as one of the two national anthems, alongside the old apartheid anthem Die Stem van Suid Afrika ("The Call of South Africa"). Later, a single anthem was created incorporating verses in Xhosa, the Zulu translation of Nkosi Sikelele, Sotho, Afrikaans and English. The original hymn in translation is still the anthem of Zambia and Tanzania. Zimbabwe and Namibia have since changed their anthems.

⚔️ QUIZ FORMAT: “Guru–Sishya Challenge”
👥 Team Structure
Each team: 3 members — 1 Guru + 2 Sishyas
Roles:
Guru: Mentor who can give limited hints.
Sishya 1 & 2: Active players who take turns answering.
---
🎮 Gameplay
1️⃣ Rounds
Total: 50 questions divided into multiple rounds (e.g., 5 rounds of 10 questions each)
Each round can have a theme or difficulty level (General Knowledge, History, Science, Audio-Visual, Rapid Fire, etc.)
---
2️⃣ Tag Team Rules
Start: Sishya 1 begins answering.
Tag Rule:
If Sishya 1 is stumped on a question, they can tag Sishya 2.
Once tagged, Sishya 2 must stay for at least 5 questions before tagging back.
Tagging is strategic — only allowed between questions, not mid-question.
The Guru cannot answer but can advise when to tag or use a hint.
---
3️⃣ Guru’s Hint Power
The Guru can give one hint for every 5 questions.
Example: For Q1–5 → 1 hint total
Hints can be used at any question within that block.
Once a hint is used in that block, the next 5 questions cannot receive another.
The hint must be concise and cryptic — no direct answers.
---
4️⃣ Question Format
All questions are multiple choice (A, B, C, D).
Each correct answer = 10 points
Wrong answer = 0 points (no negatives, unless you want a competitive twist like –5)
---
5️⃣ Head-On Challenge Round (Finale)
Top 2 teams enter a Head-On Duel.
Both teams face the same set of 10 tough questions.
Buzz-in style: First to buzz answers.
Wrong buzz = –10 penalty; Correct = +20.
Guru cannot help in this round — Sishyas only!
---
🏆 Scoring Example
Round	Total Qs	Points per Q	Hints	Max Points
Round 1	10	10	2	100
Round 2	10	10	2	100
Round 3	10	10	2	100
Round 4	10	10	2	100
Round 5 (Head-On)	10	20	0	200
Total possible: 600 points
---
⚙️ Optional Twists
Guru’s Gamble: Guru can “sacrifice” one future hint to double points for the current question.
Silent Round: One round where Guru cannot speak or signal — full test for Sishyas.
Tag Lock: If a team tags more than 3 times in a round, they lose their next hint opportunity.
--- ‎<This message was edited>

X was a ship that is powered entirely by sail, and prioritizes maneuverability at the expense of size and armament strength. By the end of this war, the Dutch navy had replaced all its heavy ships with the lighter Xs. At this time, the term X meant any sailing warship carrying fewer than 40 guns. The term dropped out of use in the second half of the 19th century, and made a comeback in WW2 to describe an escort ship of intermediate size. ID X.
